---
title: "Exercise 3: Read a SQL diff"
description: "Change a query and compare the code diff with the output."
---

**Goal**: see why keeping logic in plain-text files (`.sql`, `.R`, `.qmd`) makes changes easy to review, and binary outputs (`.xlsx`) don't.

## 1. Branch and edit the query

1. Create a branch `alex/rate-precision` from an up-to-date `main`.
2. Open `sql/data_table.sql`. It builds the Excel table each focus area offers for download.
3. Make two changes: show the rate to two decimal places, and rename the column.

```sql
-- before
  round(100 * s.numerator / s.denominator, 1) AS "Rate (%)"
-- after
  round(100 * s.numerator / s.denominator, 2) AS "Rate (per cent)"
```

## 2. Look at the diff

::: {.panel-tabset group="ide"}
## RStudio

Git pane → select `sql/data_table.sql` → **Diff**.

## Positron

Source Control → click `data_table.sql`. The side-by-side view highlights the changed characters within the line.

## Terminal

```bash
git diff --word-diff sql/data_table.sql
```

`--word-diff` shows exactly which words changed inside a line.
:::

One line changed, and a reviewer can see exactly how.

## 3. Compare with the output

Render the page and open the Excel download:

```bash
quarto render bowel-cancer.qmd
```

`downloads/bowel_participation.xlsx` has changed too, but Git can't show you how: `.xlsx` is a binary (zipped) format. This is why the repository ignores `downloads/` and keeps the query instead. The query is the thing to review; the spreadsheet is rebuilt from it.

## 4. Discard or commit

If you want to keep the change, commit and push it as in Exercise 1. Otherwise throw it away:

::: {.panel-tabset group="ide"}
## RStudio

Git pane → right-click `sql/data_table.sql` → **Revert...** → **Yes**.

## Positron

Source Control → hover over the file → **Discard Changes** (curved arrow) → **Discard File**.

## Terminal

```bash
git restore sql/data_table.sql
```
:::
